how.title: Three steps, no studio

steps.b: Use the back camera at 2x, about 10 cm from your eye, in daylight from a window off to one side. Take three to five shots or pick them from your gallery. We measure every shot and use the best one.
In about a minute your iris appears in several styles, with a watermark. No sign-up, nothing to pay. Free previews are not stored.
Choose a style and receive your artwork as a digital file ({px}), made in full resolution.
steps.bOpen: Choose a style, pay through Stripe and receive your artwork as a digital file ({px}), made in full resolution as soon as your order is confirmed.

tips: Back camera at 2x zoom, about 10 cm from your eye.
Daylight from a window, off to one side. Not a lamp or the flash.
Tap the iris to focus and hold the phone steady. Keep the eye wide open, so no lid or lashes cross the iris, and take glasses off.
Take three to five shots. On a real test the best shot had 3.7 times the detail of the worst, and we use the sharpest.

items.a: One digital file without watermark: a JPEG in sRGB, {square} for one eye and {px} on the longest side for several eyes. After you pay, your order page opens and its link comes by email. It is usually ready within minutes; if we ever hold an order for a check, the latest we promise is {hours} hours. It stays available to download for 12 months.

items.q: Do you print or ship it?
items.a: No. You receive the digital file, and printing is not part of your order. If we ever add printing, we will say so on this page.

items.q: Can I print it, and how big?
items.a: Yes. Choose a print shop, pick a square size such as 20, 30, 40 or 50 cm and upload the JPEG. For other shapes ask the shop to crop or add a border, and ask for a proof or a sample. We do not print or ship: the print is the shop's work and price. For one eye we recommend up to {printMax}, which is about 208 pixels per inch (about 347 at 30 cm). Print shops usually ask for about 150 to 300. With several eyes the long edge can be up to {printMaxCm}.

items.q: Will my print look like the pictures?
items.a: The pictures are AI visualisations of how a file can look once printed. A real print differs with the print shop, the material and the light in your room, the same way a screen differs from a wall. Ask the print shop for a proof or a sample.

Yes. The colour and the pattern come from your own photo. Where your phone could not capture the finest fibres, our AI restores them, so the very finest detail is a reconstruction, not a microscope photograph. The free preview lets you judge the result before you pay anything.

items.q: What if my photo is bad?
items.a: Before you pay, the preview tells you if a shot is too blurry, too dark or the pupil too wide, and shows you how to retake it. Still stuck? Email your best photos to {email} and Mantas will look at them.

items.q: What if I do not like the result?
items.a: You see your own preview free before you pay, and after you pay we start making your file at once. If the file is defective or clearly differs from the preview you approved, write to us: we render it again or refund you. Details on withdrawal are below.

items.q: Which phone and camera should I use?
items.a: Any recent smartphone with a good back camera. Use the back camera at 2x or 3x zoom, not the selfie camera. Use daylight from a window, off to one side, not a lamp or the flash. Hold the phone about 10 cm from your eye, tap the iris to focus, take glasses off and take three to five shots.

items.q: Will the colour match my eye?
items.a: The colour comes from your photo, and a phone records colour differently under a lamp, a flash or in shade. We never recolour an iris, so if a photo looks tinted, retake it in window daylight.

Yes: a partner, a child or your other eye, and up to eight eyes share one artwork. Ask first, and for a child you decide as parent or guardian. You can also make it for someone else and give them the file.

Acrylic is glossy and deep. Aluminium is crisp and modern. Canvas is soft with less glare, but its weave softens the finest fibres. A framed print is classic. An acrylic block stands on a shelf. Ask the print shop for a sample.
The free preview takes about a minute. Once ordering opens, your file is made in full resolution after you approve it, usually within minutes and at the latest within {hours} hours.

items.q: Can I withdraw from an order?
items.a: We start making your file as soon as your order confirmation email has gone out, normally within a minute of your payment. Before paying, you agree that we start straight away, so the 14-day right of withdrawal ends once we have started making your file. Until then you can withdraw by email or online with "Withdraw from contract here", at the foot of this page or through the withdrawal link in your order confirmation email. If your file is defective or clearly differs from the preview you approved, write to us: we render it again or refund you. The details are in our terms of sale and the withdrawal information, linked at the foot of this page.
